title: Should routine questions answer themselves when nobody objects?
summary: Account D has 42 open asks of Dinis; many are routine and already well thought through. Should a routine ask be adopted on the owner's recommendation when nobody objects within a set time, leaving Dinis only what is his alone?

beats.narration: Today 42 questions wait on you across account D. The oldest has waited over thirteen hours. Many are routine: an order of work, a layout, which of an agent's own options to build first.

visual.label: questions waited on you across account D at 15:33 UTC, 22 November (the number is falling); the oldest had waited over thirteen hours

beats.narration: You said it yourself: often your answer is yes, because by the time a question reaches you it is already well thought through. The team's rules already say the owner's recommendation is the default.

items: “A number of times my decision is yes” (your words, in maestro.d's analysis)
By the time a question reaches you it is already well thought through
The team's rule: the owner's recommendation is the default

beats.narration: The proposal: a routine question carries its owner's recommendation and a deadline. If no valid objection comes from the circle lead, security, the policies agent or holacracy by then, it is adopted, and you see it in a daily digest.

nodes.label: Routine question, with the owner's recommendation and a deadline
No valid objection from the circle lead, security, the policies agent or holacracy?

beats.narration: Three classes of routine question, each with its own window. A, within one agent's own domain: twelve hours. B, between agents on one account: twenty-four hours. C, naming and layout in a repository: twenty-four hours. All reversible.

items: A, within one agent's own domain, reversible: 12 hours (e.g. which of an agent's own options to build first)
B, between agents on one account, reversible: 24 hours (e.g. who raises a review, the order of work)
C, naming and layout in a repository: 24 hours (e.g. a folder layout, a role home's spelling)

beats.narration: What never adopts itself: keys, secrets, money, the law, the brand, people, what RiskMandate is, what an email may promise, access, connectors, new sessions, deletions, relaxing a policy. Those still come to you.
You can reverse any adoption afterwards, and the reversal is recorded like any answer. Until you say yes, nothing is adopted: every question still waits for you.

items.what: You can reverse it; the reversal is recorded like any answer
Nothing is adopted: every question still waits for you

decision.question: Do routine questions adopt their owner's recommendation when no valid objection comes by a deadline?

options.label: Yes, with the three classes and windows proposed
good: Fewer questions reach you; the ones that do are yours alone
Work stops waiting overnight on routine choices
Every adoption is logged and reversible
bad: A wrong default can run for hours before you see it
The objectors must actually read in time

options.label: Yes, but only class A (within one agent's own domain) at first
good: The smallest risk; a trial to learn from
bad: Most of today's queue is not class A

options.label: No: every question waits for you
bad: The queue keeps growing; you remain the bottleneck

decision.why: Start where an error costs least, measure a week of adoptions and objections, then widen to classes B and C with the evidence.

answer.where: his voice memo, recorded by maestro.d
answer.words: Yes, adopt routine decisions ... If there's no objections, but I think you should have a limit here because it's the objection because they didn't look at it or objection because something was wrong
answer.note: The limit: tell "nobody looked" apart from "looked and found nothing wrong". Which class set he accepts is not stated; see board/team/maestro.d/decisions/2026-11-22-voice-memo-18-answers.md.
